reference_memory.normal_pattern: The normal pattern consists of sharp, symmetric triangular pulses recurring at a stable period of approximately 5 points (consistent with the estimated period of 5 and window_cycles scaling). Each pulse rises rapidly from near-zero baseline to a peak (robust standardized value 20–42), then falls sharply back to baseline within ~2 points, followed by a flat or slightly rising quiescent interval (~3 points) before the next pulse. Baseline is near zero (median ≈ -0.4 to 0.07), with low noise during quiescence (MAD 0.14–0.25 in short windows, up to 0.48 in longer ones due to inclusion of pulse transitions). Peak amplitudes vary (20–42), but morphology—steep linear ascent/descent, apex symmetry, and consistent width—is highly repeatable. Curvature is high at peaks (23–25) and near-zero elsewhere; roughness is low in quiescent phases (<0.5) but spikes during transitions. No sustained trend is present across candidates; slope_per_point values are near zero except in candidate 3 where a spurious large slope (1.76) arises from endpoint truncation, not true drift. Acceptable variation includes moderate amplitude modulation and minor baseline offsets, but pulse shape, periodicity, and quiescent flatness are invariant.
